title: Coastline ChatLab — Account Snapshot (2026-03-18)
primary_contact: Product lead (name redacted in notes) + DevOps lead
account_overview: Inbound SMB lead via blog post on "cheap LLMs for support". Self-serve signup completed 2026-02-20; usage increased after discovery. Team is small but technical (product + fullstack + devops). Primary evaluation criteria remain: (1) user-facing answer quality for support chat, (2) predictable cost at scale, (3) latency consistency on hosted API, (4) SOC2 + SSO readiness. They want a recommended "default + fallback" routing approach (fast 7B for most turns; higher-quality model for escalations / long context).
what_changed_since_last_snapshot: Since 2026-03-05: (a) security review progressed after we shared SOC2 package under NDA, (b) pricing discussion moved from rough per-1k tokens to a concrete pilot worksheet with their traffic assumptions, (c) we provided preliminary hosted API latency benchmarks and clarified p95 expectations, (d) they asked for an embeddings plan + index sizing guidance (KB + transcripts). Close date slipped from April to May to accommodate their internal security sign-off window.
current_blockers: Need final confirmation that SOC2 report + subprocessor list satisfies procurement (legal review in progress)
Wants clearer guidance on p95 latency variability during incident-like traffic bursts
Needs a concrete recommended model lineup from our hosted catalog (names/tiers) including a fallback policy
Asks for best-practice token minimization templates for support chat (to keep spend within pilot budget)
resolved_or_improved_blockers: SOC2 evidence: provided 2026-03-12 (SOC2 Type II report + bridge letter where applicable) — no longer a hard stop, now in review
Token pricing confusion: aligned on a shared worksheet and agreed to estimate with a mix of short-turn traffic + occasional long summaries
latency_and_throughput_targets: Customer target remains 150–300ms p50 for short chat turns (<= ~200 output tokens) with stable tail latency; concurrency usually 20–50, with bursts up to ~150 concurrent for <30 minutes during incidents. They explicitly asked to understand p95 under burst conditions and whether we can reserve capacity or recommend backpressure/queueing patterns.
hosted_api_latency_notes_internal: Preliminary numbers shared (directional, not SLA): for a small/fast instruction model in our hosted tier, p50 for short answers typically lands ~200–280ms with p95 ~600–900ms depending on prompt size and regional load. For a higher-quality fallback model, p50 often ~350–550ms with p95 ~1.2–2.0s on comparable prompts. We should re-check with infra for the current week’s p95 in NA region and ensure we caveat these as benchmark ranges, not contractual.
cost_sensitivity_and_pricing_notes: Very cost-sensitive. Their stated goal is to keep annual hosted spend under ~$50k at pilot scale. They are open to paying more for escalations if (a) most traffic stays on a cheaper default model and (b) we can show routing reduces blended cost. They asked for a "blended cost" example: 80–90% requests on a low-cost model; 10–20% on a premium model for ambiguous intent/long context. They also want to use Optimize features (caching, batching where applicable, prompt/token trimming guidance) to reduce unit cost.
model_preferences_and_questions: They continue to compare Llama vs Mistral vs Qwen families. Key asks: (1) recommend a default fast model for chat and a fallback model for quality, (2) explain quantized vs non-quantized tradeoffs and how that shows up in hosted performance, (3) provide a simple routing heuristic (confidence/length/intent) and a minimal sample app. New: they asked whether embeddings should be generated with a separate model than the chat model, and how to handle ticket transcript chunking + refresh cadence.
security_and_compliance_details: Requires SOC2 evidence, SSO (SAML or OIDC) integration, audit logs, and retention controls. Data residency not strict today; they prefer NA processing. No air-gapped/on-prem requirement now; they mentioned they might revisit Dedicated next year only if they add regulated customers. Action item: confirm SSO approach (Okta vs Azure AD) and whether they need SCIM in phase 2 (they hinted it might be needed later but not for pilot).
next_step: Deliver v2 one-page recommendation (model lineup + routing policy) + confirm updated hosted-API benchmark ranges; schedule 45-min technical deep dive with their DevOps lead.

They also emphasized that hallucination risk on escalations is the key reason they’re willing to pay more for a fallback model.
